newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-S&P affirms Tasmania rating at AA-/A1+.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-S&P affirms Tasmania rating at AA-/A1+.

text.p: Standard and Poors Corp said on Wednesday it had affirmed its AA-minus long term and A-1+ short term local and foreign currency debt ratings of the government of the Australian state of Tasmania.
S&P said it had also affirmed the same local and foreign currency ratings on the Tasmanian Public Finance Corporation (Tascorp). It said the ratings outlooks were stable.

"The ratings reflect a debt burden above the average of other Australian states, a sustainable ongoing financial position and a commitment to a disciplined medium-term fiscal framework, and the state's narrow economic base," S&P said.
"The supportive fiscal arrangements between the federal and state governments in Australia also underpin the ratings."
S&P said Tasmania's net indebtedness had fallen consistently over the past decade to 116 percent of revenue as of June 30, 1996 from 153 percent at June 30, 1990.

"However, it is still the highest of the Australian states and is well above the 56 percent net debt-to-revenue ratio for the Australian state sector as a whole at June 30, 1996," it said. The ratings agency said about 40 percent of the state's debt relates to the Hydro-Electric Corporation, reflecting the capital intensive nature of the state's hydro-electric system.
General government sector net debt at June 30, 1996 was a manageable 70 percent of revenue, although this was also high in comparision to other states, S&P said.
"The state's ongoing financial position is now strong, with fiscal 1997 expected to be the third year in a row when the total state sector records an underlying surplus," S&P said.
"The government has committed itself to a fiscal strategy that implies that the general government sector will record at least some surpluses in the three fiscal years to June 2000."
S&P said the economy, dependent on natural resources and the overall world economy, was subdued in 1996 with falls in gross state product, employment and business investment.
It said the outlook was stable.

"The state's ongoing finances are established in a sustainable position and the government is committed to a fiscal strategy that will see continuing reductions in the debt burden indicators which could be accelerated by the proposed sale of parts of the Hydro-Electric Corporation," the agency said.
"However, the state's economic performance is expected to remain below the national average," it said.
